subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable batching/aggregation of outbound Telegram notifications

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in outbound Telegram notification digest policy, and should that policy live in shared outbound delivery, the bundled Telegram plugin, or an external plugin/hook surface?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear from source, but the right contract affects config shape, delivery timing, urgent error bypass, media/thread semantics, persistence, and OpenClaw's core-versus-plugin boundary.

options.title: Define an opt-in durable digest policy
options.body: Choose the shared or Telegram-owned seam, config names, bypass rules, and SQLite-backed flush behavior before implementation.

options.title: Require an external plugin or hook extension
options.body: Keep core lean and first extend or document the plugin hook contract if durable delayed aggregation cannot be built safely with today’s seams.

options.title: Keep immediate delivery
options.body: Treat current streaming coalescing, error cooldowns, and throttling as the supported anti-spam mechanisms and close or narrow this request.

recommendation.title: Define an opt-in durable digest policy
recommendation.body: Choose the shared or Telegram-owned seam, config names, bypass rules, and SQLite-backed flush behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current-history routing candidate across the Telegram outbound adapter, shared durable send path, throttler, and config surface involved in this product decision.
